cluster_summary: This cluster encompasses vulnerabilities where server-side code fails to implement proper cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protections, perform necessary authorization checks, or employ correct security context handling. These flaws allow attackers to forge requests, escalate privileges, or bypass access controls.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add CSRF token generation, embed in forms or headers, and validate on the server side before processing.
sub_patterns.name: Missing synchronizer token (CSRF token) on state-changing requests
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application relies solely on cookie-based authentication without a server-generated token that must be submitted with each state-changing request, allowing cross-site request forgery.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Insert an explicit permission check (e.g., hasAccess) after CSRF validation.
sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization check after CSRF token validation
sub_patterns.root_cause: The endpoint validates CSRF tokens but fails to verify the user holds the required permission (e.g., programming rights) before executing the action.
